transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Liam O'Shea (Head of ML, Oceanic); Nora Diaz (Platform Engineer, Oceanic); Carla Mendes (Head of Product, Oceanic)

Summary: quick discovery to align on budget lanes and decide whether to trial hosted or reserved (dedicated) capacity. High-level budget cap: $45k/month for inference initially. Latency SLO: 95th < 250ms for short prompts (~150 tokens). Key ask: sample cost workbook and a 2-model bench that demonstrates batching/caching gains and private deployment constraints.

Topics covered: pricing levers, batching and prefix/K-V cache, dedicated pool sizing, private/VPC considerations, SOC 2 and data residency, pilot scope and next steps.

[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intro from our side — I'm Ethan, AE, and Priya's our SE who will do the deeper numbers.
[00:18] Liam (Oceanic): hey thanks, Liam here — head of ML. We run the checkout assistant and an internal insights agent, um, both are fairly token heavy but the checkout flow has the stricter latency needs.
[00:30] Nora (Oceanic): Nora — platform, I'll be owning infra constraints. we have a hard monthly inference budget right now, roughly 45k, maybe a little flexible if ROI is clear.
[00:40] Carla (Oceanic): Carla — product. main metric is conversion lift; tolerated latency at checkout is tight.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): great, thanks. first question, what are your current qps and sequence lengths for the checkout assistant? even ballpark helps.
[01:05] Liam: peak qps is about 40 rps for the assistant; typical reply is 120 tokens, sometimes up to 250. The insight agent is lower qps but larger contexts.
[01:20] Priya: ok, 40rps peak — good to know. our main levers to hit cost/latency are batching, prefix/KV cache and model selection/quantization. as we talk about hosted vs dedicated we'll map those levers to unit cost.
[01:40] Ethan: and on financing, hosted is pay-as-you-go — simple per-token; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. private adds VPC + audit needs.
[02:05] Nora: on private, we can't expose PII off-prem for a subset of requests; payments tokens and PII need to stay in our VPC. can dedicated run in our cloud region?
[02:20] Priya: yes — dedicated can be region pinned, and Private deployment is our package for VPC-only control plane. but it does change the economics — reserved cost plus infra.
[02:35] Carla: what about fallback? if dedicated is full, will hosted be an option?
[02:45] Ethan: good question — standard pattern is routing policy with fallback to hosted or a cheaper model variant. we'll include that in the workbook scenarios.
[03:10] Priya: quick demo of cost levers — so, base per-token for the model family you mentioned (we talked about using a 13B class) is X cents/token for hosted. However batching at 4–8 requests can bring effective per-token down 20–40% depending on token distribution. cache hit rate on prefixes for the checkout flow can be substantial — if 30% of requests reuse prefixes, cost drops and latency improves for cache hits.
[03:50] Liam: can you unpack the cache? our prompts have a repetitive prefix for user/cart state — will that map to hits?
[04:05] Priya: yeah so prefix caching stores KV cache for common prefixes; warmup cost is real though, initial requests pay the full cost. we sometimes see K-V pronounced "K V cash" in notes — sorry for the speech — but the mechanics are the same.
[04:20] Nora: warmup — how many tokens or requests to warm a cache line?
[04:30] Priya: depends, but for checkout style prompts you can see benefit after a few dozen similar requests; warmup cost ~first N tokens per unique prefix. we'll export a small synthetic benchmark that shows warmup curves.
[05:00] Carla: and batching — our UX requires single-turn latency under 250ms most of the time. batching helps cost but increases latency; is there a sweet spot?
[05:15] Priya: yes, if you can tolerate ~30–60ms extra p95, batching at 2–3 can buy a lot; beyond that you start to see tail hurts. with our dedicated pools you can configure continuous batching windows to trade latency for throughput predictably.
[05:45] Ethan: I'll add an explicit latency vs cost chart in the workbook. we'll show a hosted baseline and dedicated reserved pool examples.
[06:05] Liam: what's the rough delta between hosted and dedicated monthly for our qps? ballpark only.
[06:20] Priya: very rough — with your numbers (40rps peak; 120 tokens avg) hosted might run you in the 30–50k/month range depending on model choice and cache hits. dedicated, with a 3–6 GPU reserved pool and efficient batching, could be 20–35k/month amortized, but there's an upfront commit and ops overhead. private on-prem will be higher still due to infra and support.
[06:50] Nora: hmm that matches our gut. is there a minimum committed capacity for Dedicated?
[06:58] Ethan: we do monthly reserved commands; minimal pool is often sized around 2–3 cards depending on model. we'll model a 3-card and 6-card baseline in the workbook.
[07:20] Carla: about SLA — do you guarantee p95 latency and what happens if we breach?
[07:30] Priya: for Dedicated we have SLA backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort SLOs with credits. for enterprise private we can negotiate SLA terms. also we provide tracing and per-route dashboards in the console.
[07:55] Liam: security—SOC 2, SSO, KMS for keys?
[08:05] Ethan: we are SOC 2 Type II; we integrate with SAML/SSO and can support customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private deployments. we'll attach the security deck and SOC 2 letter.
[08:25] Nora: great. For the pilot we want to bench two models: a smaller low-latency 7B and a 13B quality model. can you recommend tokenization and prompt slices?
[08:40] Priya: yes, we'll propose a 3-prompt set (checkout short, checkout with product details, and a long insight query). we'll run a 2-day pilot and measure p50/p95 latency, batch sizes, cache hit rate and cost per 1k responses.
[09:10] Carla: timeline — how quickly can the pilot start?
[09:20] Ethan: assuming we get infra alignment, we can stand up hosted pilot in a few days. Dedicated pilot / private will take longer due to provisioning — estimate 2–3 weeks.
[09:40] Liam: we want eyes on the math — can you show a worked example in the call?
[09:48] Priya: sure — quick example: with hosted price of 0.0025 $/token (example), 120 tokens per request, that's 0.30 $/request raw. at 40 rps sustained that's 1,036,800 requests/month ~ $311k — wait, that seems off, hang on — arithmetic slip — sorry. let's recalibrate live.
[10:10] Priya: correct calc: 40 rps peak doesn't mean sustained 24/7—if average is 10 rps sustained, that'd be 864k requests/mo. multiply 0.30 per req ~ $259k, still high. so we need batching and cache to get down to target. at batching factor 3 and 30% cache hit reducing effective tokens, you can get ~3–4x reduction.
[10:50] Ethan: that's why modeling usage patterns is key; your budget cap of $45k/mo suggests starting hybrid: hosted for burst + dedicated reserved for steady baseline.
[11:10] Nora: do you have customers who did hybrid routing?
[11:15] Ethan: yes; a couple of retail customers use dedicated for daytime peak and hosted for off-hours/burst. routing policies and automatic fallback are in the console.
[11:35] Liam: any examples of quantization impact? cost vs quality?
[11:45] Priya: 8-bit quantization for 13B models often preserves quality for chat prompts but some edge cases need fp16. quantized variants lower GPU memory and can increase packing/batch efficiency which indirectly reduces cost. tradeoff depends on your eval set.
[12:10] Carla: so the workbook should show hosted, dedicated, and private columns with sample numbers and assumptions.
[12:15] Ethan: yes exactly. we'll include sensitivity knobs: average tokens, cache hit, batch factor, model variant.
[12:30] Liam: on residency: can dedicated be in eu-west-1 only for certain routes? we need EU residency for EU users.
[12:40] Priya: yes route-level region pinning is supported. you can pin requests by header or route to run in EU-only pools. Private gives you even tighter controls.
[13:00] Nora: network egress costs—are those in your pricing?
[13:10] Ethan: hosted pricing often includes egress to the same region; cross-region or external egress may be billed. we'll call that out in the workbook.
[13:35] Carla: what's the onboarding timeline and technical requirements for private deployment?
[13:45] Priya: Private requires customer-managed networking, a local runtime deployment, and access to your KMS if required. typical timelines 4–8 weeks depending on approvals.
[14:05] Liam: ok. let's talk about pilot acceptance criteria — what defines success?
[14:15] Ethan: pilot success usually: 1) meet p95 latency < 250ms on checkout prompt, 2) costs per 1k responses below target (we'll let you define target), 3) no functional regressions on key prompts.
[14:40] Carla: our target cost is under $0.40 per 100 requests for checkout — kinda arbitrary but that's our starting point.
[14:55] Priya: we'll translate that into tokens and effective per-token target in the workbook.
[15:12] Liam: any blockers from our side? Nora: infra will need IP allowlist and an API key rotation policy; we prefer SSO gating.
[15:25] Ethan: that's fine. we support IP allowlisting and SAML; we'll share the security doc.
[15:40] Priya: quick note on evaluation: warmup distortions in short pilots can overstate cost. we'll run a synthetic ramp to estimate steady-state cache hit rates.
[16:05] Carla: great, that helps.
[16:15] Ethan: recap on next steps: we'll send workbook and security docs, propose pilot dates, and Priya will attach benchmark artifacts.
[16:25] Liam: when can we expect the workbook?
[16:30] Ethan: by Friday 2026-05-08.
[16:35] Nora: I'll send our qps histogram and a sample prompt set by Monday 2026-05-11.
[16:45] Priya: we'll also include a quick prioritized eval checklist so you can validate quality regressions.
[17:00] Carla: thanks, this was productive.
[17:10] Ethan: cheers — we'll follow up with the workbook and SOC 2 artifact.

Action items (recap in call):
- Ethan: send tailored cost workbook and hosted/dedicated/private example scenarios (due 2026-05-08)
- Priya: attach KV-cache benchmark, warmup notes, and small synthetic bench artifacts (due 2026-05-07)
- Nora: share qps histogram and sample prompt set (due 2026-05-11)

Closing notes: Customer leaning toward a hybrid pilot: dedicated baseline for steady-state and hosted for bursts. Big decision hinges on whether dedicated's amortized cost hits their $45k/mo ceiling after batching/cache gains. Redwood will provide sensitivity workbook and run a 2-model short pilot to demonstrate economics.
questions: What are your realistic sustained rps and average tokens?
Are there hard data residency constraints per route?
Do you have a target cost-per-1000 responses to validate pilot success?
